body:
### Summary

`uv pip install` has some strange output relating to yanked releases.

Running this:
```bash
uv venv -p 3.13
uv pip install 'aprict<=0.1.0'
```

Produces this output:
```
error: No solution found when resolving dependencies
  cause: Because aprict==0.0.24.dev1 was yanked (reason: Error in version number (should have been
         0.0.25)) and aprict==0.0.34.dev8 was yanked (reason: Failed version bump (should have been
         updated to v0.0.35)), we can conclude that all of:
             aprict==0.0.24.dev1
             aprict==0.0.34.dev8
          cannot be used. (1)

         Because the current Python version (3.13.16) does not satisfy Python>=3.14 and all of:
             aprict<=0.0.23
             aprict>=0.0.24,<=0.0.33
             aprict>=0.0.34,<=0.1.0
         depend on Python>=3.14, we can conclude that all of:
             aprict<=0.0.23
             aprict>=0.0.24,<=0.0.33
             aprict>=0.0.34,<=0.1.0
          cannot be used.
         And because only the following versions of aprict are available:
             aprict<=0.0.23
             aprict==0.0.24.dev1
             aprict>=0.0.24,<=0.0.33
             aprict==0.0.34.dev8
             aprict>=0.0.34
         we can conclude that all of:
             aprict<0.0.24.dev1
             aprict>0.0.24.dev1,<0.0.34.dev8
             aprict>0.0.34.dev8,<=0.1.0
          cannot be used.
         And because we know from (1) that all of:
             aprict==0.0.24.dev1
             aprict==0.0.34.dev8
          cannot be used, we can conclude that aprict<=0.1.0 cannot be used.
         And because you require aprict<=0.1.0, we can conclude that your requirements are
```

This output is overly noisy and quite misleading, because *all* versions of this module, including the yanked releases, require `Python>=3.14`. I find that the output above strongly implies that the yanked versions might work if they were downloaded and manually installed. This might lead a user to waste their time trying to source versions of the module which could be compatible with `Python==3.13`.

My guess is that the reason this is happening is that `uv` is checking for reasons why the package versions can't be installed, and is checking first for whether a version is yanked, and is returning early on that check before anything else. I'd suggest that `uv` should also check whether a module version *would* be installable if it weren't yanked, and should only mentioned the yanked versions if being yanked is the sole thing preventing them from being installed.

### Platform

Linux 7.2.8-arch1-2 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.12.22 (70fe1196a 2026-10-01 x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

Python 3.13.16
title: Misleading version constraint output from `uv pip install`
